name: Rates of Intimate Partner Violence Across New York City: An Intersectional Analysis
description:
This dataset contains counts of intimate partner violence (IPV) assaults across New York City, broken down by race/ethnicity and sex, alongside population counts for the same groups. Each of the 61 rows represents a geographic location—the citywide total plus individual areas such as the Bronx, Brooklyn, Manhattan, and Queens—with 36 columns covering population size, observed assault counts, and expected assault counts for White, Black, Hispanic, Asian/Pacific Islander, and American Indian groups, each further split into female and male categories.

The observed assault columns record actual reported IPV incidents for each demographic group, while the expected_assault columns provide a comparison baseline (likely derived from population proportions), allowing users to assess whether violence rates are higher or lower than would be anticipated given group size. Population columns give the underlying denominators needed to calculate rates per capita.

The data supports intersectional analysis of IPV disparities—examining how race/ethnicity and gender combine to shape risk across neighborhoods. It
